design_promise: Weapons are profitable goods whose movement changes the political map; the player can trade arms, but cannot pretend the cargo has no owner or consequence.

state_axes.meaning: The Cinder Riders’ capacity to protect routes, coerce rivals, and become a major regional power.
The Salt Crown’s capacity to defend wells, enforce cistern law, and dominate water access.
The region’s visible level of confrontation, from tense border trade to open war.
How much local settlements believe either tribe is protecting people rather than accumulating power.

weapon_goods.name: Scrap Blades
weapon_goods.notes: The most accessible arms good. Useful for defending caravans, but easy to move through unofficial routes.

weapon_goods.name: Reed Bows
weapon_goods.notes: Supports frontier defense and escort work, but can arm small bands quickly.

weapon_goods.name: Salt-Crown Lamellar
weapon_goods.notes: Expensive protection that makes a faction harder to dislodge and signals a serious military commitment.

weapon_goods.name: Powder Components
weapon_goods.notes: Rare and dangerous. A shipment can change the conflict quickly, but attracts inspections, theft, and retaliation.

preserve_frontier_trade: Weapon goods use the same buy, carry, route, demand, and sell loop as ordinary goods.
The player can still profit without selling weapons by carrying water, grain, medicine, scrap, charcoal, or cloth.
Weapons should be high-margin alternatives, not strictly better commodities.
Weapon prices rise with conflict, but route risk, inspections, shortages, and political consequences rise with them.
A weapon sale changes faction power only when the shipment reaches a buyer; buying weapons does not cause invisible escalation.
arms_trade_rules.power_formula: buyer_armed_power increases by direct_power_effect modified by shipment_size, delivery_success, and existing_power_gap
arms_trade_rules.conflict_formula: tribal_conflict increases when both tribes gain arms, when a high-risk shipment is intercepted, or when a faction’s power gap crosses a visible threshold
arms_trade_rules.legitimacy_formula: tribal_legitimacy increases through protection, fair distribution, and mediation; it decreases when arms are used for coercion, blockade, or settlement intimidation
arms_trade_rules.no_hidden_effects: The player must receive a report after a weapon delivery explaining whether the shipment strengthened escorts, escalated a rivalry, or was diverted.

escalation_stages.name: Uneasy Trade
escalation_stages.weapon_behavior: Arms are legal or tolerated, and both tribes seek small defensive shipments.
escalation_stages.failure_cost: A local escort becomes less reliable or a settlement becomes suspicious.

escalation_stages.name: Armed Escorts
escalation_stages.weapon_behavior: Small arms improve route protection, but weapon buyers start competing for supply.
escalation_stages.failure_cost: The rival increases patrols and weapon prices become more volatile.

escalation_stages.name: Contested Routes
escalation_stages.weapon_behavior: A large shipment raises armed power and can close a route if the rival feels outmatched.
escalation_stages.failure_cost: Cargo seizure, route closure, settlement resilience loss, or forced rerouting.

escalation_stages.name: Open War
escalation_stages.weapon_behavior: High-risk arms are extremely profitable but create direct risk to civilian routes and the caravan itself.
escalation_stages.failure_cost: Multiple routes close, water prices spike, and one settlement may become temporarily inaccessible.

escalation_stages.name: Regional Emergency
escalation_stages.weapon_behavior: The tribe with higher power can become a major faction, but legitimacy determines whether its control stabilizes or oppresses the region.
escalation_stages.failure_cost: A faction dominates a key resource and the final campaign conditions harden.

escalation_stages.name: The New Order
escalation_stages.weapon_behavior: A tribe has become a major regional power, a coalition has formed, or both tribes have exhausted their ability to continue.
escalation_stages.failure_cost: The player inherits a profitable but politically narrow market or a region with long recovery debt.

tribal_relationships.shared_interest: Both need water, scrap, and safe movement through the basin.
tribal_relationships.irreconcilable_pressure: The Cinder Riders reject permanent cistern control; the Salt Crown rejects unregulated armed movement.

conflict_events.title: A Weapon Has a Buyer
conflict_events.setup: A Cinder Rider and a Salt Crown representative both offer cash for the same crate of scrap blades. Neither asks what the other has offered.

choices.label: Sell the blades to the Cinder Riders.
choices.visible_result: The Riders can protect the Old Road, but the Salt Crown begins watching your cargo.

choices.label: Sell the blades to the Salt Crown.
choices.visible_result: The wells gain a stronger guard, but the Cinder Riders see a rival gaining leverage.

choices.label: Split the shipment and disclose the rival offer.
choices.visible_result: Both sides gain a little, and both learn that the market can be made transparent.

choices.label: Offer scrap and repair tools instead of weapons.
choices.visible_result: The shipment supports infrastructure without immediately increasing armed power.

conflict_events.title: The Escort That Wasn’t Neutral
conflict_events.setup: An armed escort offers a reduced rate after your last weapon delivery. A second escort warns that the first is now part of the conflict.

choices.label: Hire the cheaper escort.
choices.visible_result: The road is safer for your caravan and less neutral for everyone else.

choices.label: Pay for a neutral mixed escort.
choices.visible_result: The caravan travels more slowly but proves that protection does not have to become allegiance.

choices.label: Travel without an escort and keep your manifest private.
choices.visible_result: You preserve neutrality at a visible cost in safety.

conflict_events.title: The Cistern Gate
conflict_events.setup: The Salt Crown offers to protect Brine Cross’s water in exchange for exclusive access through the next two market days. The Cinder Riders call it a blockade with better language.

choices.label: Accept the protected water contract.
choices.visible_result: Water reaches paying buyers reliably, while smaller traders lose access.

choices.label: Fund a neutral convoy for all settlements.
choices.visible_result: The convoy costs more than the contract but keeps the basin from becoming one faction’s reservoir.

choices.label: Sell high-risk powder components to the Cinder Riders.
choices.visible_result: The margin is extraordinary. So is the chance that the next road becomes a battlefield.

conflict_events.title: The Basin Chooses
conflict_events.setup: The two tribes send delegations to Ashgate. Each claims that one final shipment would restore order. The ledger says both are preparing for the same war.

choices.label: Back the Cinder Riders as the open-road power.
choices.visible_result: The Old Road remains open, but armed escorts become the price of movement.

choices.label: Back the Salt Crown as the basin authority.
choices.visible_result: The wells are defended and rationed, but the market now has a gatekeeper.

choices.label: Withhold weapons and force a shared water-and-road compact.
choices.visible_result: No one gets everything. The basin keeps more of its choices.

choices.label: Take the final arms contract and leave before the roads close.
choices.visible_result: The caravan leaves rich, while the region inherits the consequences of the margin.

meta_progression.principle: The long-term layer should make trading richer by adding capacity, information, and optional strategic commitments, never by replacing the act of buying and selling.

nodes.trade_value: Know whether a high price is a real shortage or a manufactured rumor.
Wait for a better market without turning storage into passive income.
Protect a chosen cargo commitment on risky routes.
Make a weapon shipment safer without making it consequence-free.
Make political cargo choices more legible before sale.
Earn less than a war contract while keeping more routes open.
Turn relationships into a recovery option rather than a passive reputation bonus.
Influence the post-crisis market without becoming its ruler.

guardrails: Do not add a second travel game on top of trade; meta upgrades should shorten friction or widen choices.
Do not make weapons the only profitable goods; ordinary trade should remain a strong route to money and progression.
Do not make faction power invisible; show shipment reports, banners, patrols, prices, and route changes.
Do not make the player responsible for every conflict outcome; tribes have internal politics and can reject or misuse a shipment.
Every high-margin arms contract needs at least one non-arms alternative with a meaningful benefit.

major_faction_outcomes.market_change: Old Road becomes open under escort culture; water remains negotiated and prices stay volatile.
major_faction_outcomes.player_trade_position: High access to frontier and escort contracts, lower official protection.

major_faction_outcomes.market_change: Water becomes stable inside the cistern system but permission and tolls become more important.
major_faction_outcomes.player_trade_position: Reliable water contracts, reduced informal trade, stronger inspection pressure.

major_faction_outcomes.market_change: No tribe dominates; shared convoys and public measures reduce extreme volatility.
major_faction_outcomes.player_trade_position: Lower peak margins but stronger recovery, access, and long-term contracts.

design_guardrails: A weapon sale must be a trade decision first and a political trigger second.
Weapon demand should rise with conflict, but route risk, inspections, and settlement needs should rise with it.
The player should be able to become wealthy without becoming a war profiteer.
A tribe becomes a major faction through both armed power and legitimacy; combat strength alone creates fear, not stable rule.
The conflict layer should create new routes, contracts, and map changes rather than pause the trading game for a separate combat campaign.
Sovereign-style meta progression should be persistent capacity and influence, not a snowball that makes early trade obsolete.
